question: A team member tries to add a custom MCP server named computer-use to give the agent a specialized screenshot tool. What should the architect expect to happen?
options: A) Claude Code loads the custom server normally and simply hides the built-in server named computer-use for the rest of that session
B) Claude Code merges the tools from the custom server directly into the built-in server's own tool set under the shared reserved name
C) Claude Code loads the custom server but silently strips its screenshot tool since that capability is presumed reserved for the built-in server
D) Claude Code rejects or skips the server because computer-use is a reserved built-in name, so the team member needs to pick a different name
correct_answers: D) Claude Code rejects or skips the server because computer-use is a reserved built-in name, so the team member needs to pick a different name
explanations: Claude Code does not silently substitute a custom server for a built-in one under a reserved name; it skips the conflicting custom entry and warns instead.
There is no field-level merging of a custom server's tools into a built-in server; a reserved-name conflict simply causes the custom entry to be skipped.
Claude Code does not selectively strip individual tools from a reserved-name server; the entire conflicting server entry is skipped at load time.

Correct. Names like workspace, claude-in-chrome, computer-use, and the Claude Preview/Browser names are reserved for Claude Code's built-in servers; a configuration using one of these names is skipped at load time with a warning, and claude mcp add rejects it outright.
